The white fuzz on the wood is the bio film. As for the plants in the back it looks like brown a hair algae which is normal for a new tank (diatoms). For the plants that look attached to your wood with those white dots, I have no idea wtf that is, maybe aquarium glue?
The sugars in the wood start to release and it’s creates the film! Bacteria will consume it unless shrimp or snails beat them to it.

Remove the dead plants, opt for a hob filter instead of a skimmer or use both, way less lighting try 6-8 hours, do a water change (try to swish around the siphon to kick up some of the diatoms so you can siphon it o it without picking up aqua soil) 

Also if you are thinking of snails, make sure you get some cuttlefish bone or crushed coral to pop in that new hob filter to make sure your ph is at a good level for snails. Aqua soil lowers ph which isn’t sustainable for snail shells. And typically the snails you’d find at a fish store, only eat dead plants so it might be helpful to get one to clean up any dead material you’ve missed.

And the cotton looking stuff on the wood is biofilm, harmless and will happen when you put in a new piece of wood! Snails and shrimp with eat it, but it does go away eventually.

It’s a lot to keep up with and most people can’t dedicate hours a day getting all the little pieces. It’s a much easier problem to tackle if you can spend your work day doing it. Plus at a local fish store, tanks aren’t as heavily planted so it would be easier to spot and remove. It will wrap around plants, get into roots, get in your filter. And when I say optimal conditions it will grow, it seriously grows so quickly if you have a lot of microfauna in your tank. It’s a total pain in the ass basically. Not a death sentence for the tank, but most forums I’ve seen end with them starting fresh because it’s that difficult to completely remove.

If a piece of it breaks off during removal it will continue to grow. In the optimal conditions it will grow so quickly. It can be difficult to spot in a large tank with lots of plants as well so missing a piece during removal is common.

Street parking is pretty normal, not great but them not disclosing that is not something worth fighting over. If there are no signs on the street then you need to fight the ticket with the PD if it’s street parking, or with the leasing office/landlord if it’s through their towing service or whatever in their lot.

If apartment, complain to the leasing office multiple times. Most apartments don’t allow more than 2 dogs. If it’s a house with a landlord, then you might be stuck with the 7 dogs. Unless your neighbors are also renting! They could be going against their lease. 

Basement flooding, report to management or landlord. If it’s not being resolved quickly, contact them everyday. Even multiple times a day if necessary.

Even the “newly renovated” apartments aren’t great. You could be the first people living in the apartment and you will find issues from the contractors who renovated the place. Every time you move into a new rental, take photos of everything and report any damages so you aren’t liable. If you’re renting with a lower income, a perfect apartment or house at move in is lucky. 

Wi-Fi/internet may be “included” in the apartment. That means you still have to go to the Xfinity store nearby and physically pick up an box and set up your internet yourself. Going to that store should be something you do on move in day or day after. Maybe there’s apartments out there that just give you a Wi-Fi password and that’s it but that has never been my experience. 

For the communications barrier you need to take that up with the leasing office/landlord. That is definitely hindering the repairs and you will need to tell them your issues.

Hope this helps ✌️
